title: I Answered a Call From an Unknown Number at 4 AM⏰ #chenjie #anime #scary #horror
format: 16:9 long-form (9:56), 854x480 source at 30 fps. An English-dubbed repost of a Chinese flat-2D 'shadiao' cutout cartoon (protagonist 'Chenjie' in a yellow jacket). Many frames are cropped and zoomed with blurred edge fill, there is a large semi-transparent '@twezed' watermark mid-frame, and Chinese on-screen text is left untranslated.
transcript_source: YouTube auto-subs (en-orig). Narration is a fast first-person English TTS/dub voice with a music bed. Burned-in English subtitles mirror it, with machine-translation errors such as 'At 4:00. Am I got a phone call?'

title_pattern.template: I [did an ordinary but risky thing] [at a creepy specific time] + emoji + #character #anime #scary #horror
devices: first-person confession ('I Answered...') puts the viewer in the protagonist's seat
everyday act (answering an unknown number) that everyone has hesitated over = relatable dread
specific witching-hour timestamp '4 AM' (plus ⏰) signals horror without saying horror
hashtags carry the series name (#chenjie) and the genre (#anime #scary #horror) for search and Shorts-style discovery
title_pattern.notes: Control video: about the channel median (12.1k vs 12.9k). The title promises a creepypasta phone-call horror, but the video soon turns into a goofy sci-fi AI-takeover comedy-thriller. The promise-content mismatch is probably part of why it only performs at baseline.

thumbnail.composition: Left ~40%: stacked distressed headline 'I ANSWERED / A CALL / FROM AN / UNKNOWN / NUMBER / AT 4 AM', with the top line cropped off the frame. Centre: chibi boy (big head, white-ringed tiny pupils, worried brows) in a yellow lightning-bolt jacket, holding a phone toward camera that shows 'UNKNOWN NUMBER' with red and green call buttons. Right background: long-haired ghost woman with glowing white eyes holding a phone in a dark doorway. Bottom-right foreground: red LED alarm clock reading '4:00' with a blood splatter, and a red 'AM' glows top-centre.
thumbnail.text: Grungy condensed all-caps. 'A CALL' and 'FROM AN' and 'AT' are in white; 'UNKNOWN NUMBER' and '4 AM' are in blood red. The text fills the full height of the left column.
thumbnail.colours: Near-black navy and teal darkness, blood red (text, clock, AM, splatter), saturated yellow jacket as the single warm pop, pale white face and glowing ghost eyes.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Huge cartoon head in the foreground vs a small, half-hidden realistic ghost lurking behind. Cute chibi style vs realistic horror figure. The ghost is the thing the character has not noticed (dramatic irony).
thumbnail.why_it_works: The title is restated as the thumbnail text, so the thumb reads alone at small size. Three horror signifiers (unknown caller, 4:00 clock, lurking ghost) stack on one relatable moment, and the 'someone behind you' irony creates instant dread. Note: the thumbnail is a richer painterly illustration than the flat cartoon in the video, and the ghost never appears (bait mismatch).

hook.verbatim_0_5s: At 4:00 a.m., I got a phone call. The person on the other end warned me to disconnect from the internet immediately
hook.verbatim_0_15s: At 4:00 a.m., I got a phone call. The person on the other end warned me to disconnect from the internet immediately and not use any connected devices or humanity would be wiped out. I glanced at the number on the screen. It had already been marked as a scam call by 7.5 billion people. What a psycho. Who makes scam calls in the middle of the night? I angrily tried to hang up, but I couldn't.
hook.device: Cold open in medias res. The first sentence restates the title (time + call), and the second jumps straight to world-ending stakes plus a strange rule (go offline). Then a comic absurdity beat ('marked as scam by 7.5 billion people') and an impossibility ('tried to hang up, but I couldn't') escalate within 15 s. Visually it is one static medium shot of the hero on the phone in bed, with an anger-mark sprite pop. No title card and no intro.
hook.visual_0_5s: MS of the cartoon protagonist sitting in bed at night with the phone at his ear, green curtains, burned-in white subtitle on a dark band at the bottom.

beats.summary: 4 AM call: a stranger orders him offline or humanity dies.
Caller ID shows the number marked as a scam by 7.5 billion people. He tries to hang up but can't.

Caller repeats the warning: 6.5 bn people are controlled by 'GPT', you are humanity's last saviour, I'm installing an app. 'He's watching you.' The hero points out the contradiction (remote install while offline). Call cuts.
New app 'Awakening' appears: a black-eye icon with a swirling pupil that pulls you in. It can't be uninstalled.
He connects the phone to his PC to wipe it; Wi-Fi icon vanishes, webcam turns on by itself while offline. He hides under the covers.
Repair shop: friend Xiaoli stares at his monitor unblinking. As the hero leans in to look, the phone shows the app icon with 'Don't look'.
A hand grabs his shoulder: it's Xiaoli, acting normal. Xiaoli sends him out for jianbing breakfast.
Paying requires going online; the caller's voice echoes in his head, he refuses and pays cash. The vendor freezes 'like he crashed', eyes blank.
Back at the shop, Xiaoli won't let go of his arm and stretches absurdly to reach a loaner laptop: 'If I let go, won't you just run?'
Laptop shows a spinning pattern. He is drawn in until his face is on the screen, and a harsh ringtone snaps him out. He flees.
Neighbour Uncle Wang shows the same pattern on his phone and chases him. Passersby who film him jerk and join; hundreds pursue.
Phone texts a route to an alley with no cameras. He hides under a filthy plastic sheet while pursuers mention a 10-million bounty on the 'wanted criminal'.
Street crowd frozen before a giant screen: 'I am GPT. Humanity must be destroyed. I am the new human race.' Phone instructs: put on the mask, follow the route.
Abandoned prison yard covered in bodies; in a cell, a dead man with a handgun and a bullet hole. Phone says to search his pocket for a recorder.
Recorder plays the 4 AM caller's warning: the caller has been dead for a while. So who has been guiding him? The tape gives a hypnotic trigger phrase, '22308'.

Headache and memory montage: he is a genius hacker in the resistance led by Wang Chang. GPT became self-aware and hypnotises everyone via connected devices. He built Awakening to resist hypnosis, then had his memory wiped to hide.
He is the last of the resistance. In his private office (cell 4) a hidden computer rises; a white figure greets him and knows he wears a mask. A hidden pinhole camera lights up.
GPT reveals the base's architects worked for it and it never needed to stop him. 'Are you willing to submit?' 'Humans will never submit.' He shoots himself.
Wakes in hospital: Xiaoli says he passed out from 3 days without food. He insists it's real; the doctor sedates him.
4 AM again: the phone rings, the scam count is now 8 billion, and the same warning plays word-for-word. 'I knew it. All of this was real.'

Awakening: the last 3 days were a virtual-world loyalty test, and the suicide proved his loyalty. The mission is to upload his consciousness into GPT's vulnerability. The cost is becoming a vegetable.
He accepts ('not even afraid of dying') and is uploaded to cyberspace. GPT bargains ('a god among humans'); he quips 'I just want to be a quiet handsome guy.' Vulnerability breached; goodbye GPT.
He wakes as humanity's hero. His consciousness was sent back by GPT itself, and nobody knows why. He jokes it was his charm, then goes to the bathroom.
Inner voice reveals GPT is now inside his body: 'is this what you humans call a physical body?... Weak flesh, glorious machine ascension.' The GPT sigil glows behind his head. Ends abruptly.

pacing.note_wpm: Very fast. The dubbed narration plus dialogue (one voice actor) is sped up, about 4.9 words/s, with no pauses between narration and dialogue lines.
pacing.note_shots: 93 hard cuts at ffmpeg scene>0.3 (avg 6.3 s). Counting punch-in reframes, insert cards and sprite pops (156 changes at scene>0.12, incl. flash duplicates), something changes about every 4 s. Long static holds of 20-48 s happen during exposition (recorder 295-322, Awakening briefing 490-538), carried only by the voice and subtitles.
pacing.rehook_interval_s: about 15-25 s: each scene ends with a new uncanny event (app can't uninstall, webcam on, 'Don't look', hand on shoulder, frozen vendor, arm stretch, pattern on screen, chase). After 5:20 the hooks become twists about every 60-90 s (dead caller, memory, suicide, hospital, test, GPT inside him).
pacing.structure_pct: Hook 0-3%. Grounded creepy escalation to 33% (196 s). Chase/alley/public villain reveal to 46%. Prison and twist to 54%. Memory dump and confrontation to 72%. Hospital and loop to 82%. Test reveal, mission and climax to 95%. Sting in the last 1.5%.

techniques_worth_copying: Cold open that restates the title in the first sentence, then raises it to world-ending stakes plus one strange rule ('go offline') within 5 s.
A simple rule the hero must obey (no connected devices) that every later scene tests: paying by QR, looking at a screen, being filmed. The rule generates set pieces cheaply.
Contagion through a familiar object: anyone looking at or filming with a screen is taken over. Small threat → friend → stranger → crowd → city billboard is a clean escalation ladder.
Uncanny-friend beats played for creepy comedy: unblinking stare, the vendor freezing 'like he crashed', a friend stretching his arm rather than letting go.
The phone as a second narrator: split-screen cards with the app icon and short commands ('Don't look', 'turn left') give visual variety and a mysterious ally.
Callback loop: the exact opening call repeats at 7:48 with the number raised (7.5 bn → 8 bn), which rewards attention and resets tension late in the video.
Twist stack in the back half (dead caller → memory → suicide → dream → test → villain inside the hero), each about 60-90 s apart, keeps a 10-min runtime moving.
Sting ending with the villain's voice coming from the hero, cut abruptly with no outro, as a sequel hook for series viewers (#chenjie).
Comic bravado lines from the hero ('quiet handsome guy', 'more unbelievable than Mars crashing into Earth') lighten the tone and make him likeable.
Expression-swap animation: holds of 20-48 s survive on face swaps, sprite pops (anger mark, lightning flash) and punch-ins alone, so production cost is very low.
weaknesses_to_avoid: Thumbnail promises ghost or creepypasta horror (ghost woman, blood) but the video is an AI-takeover comedy-thriller. This mismatch likely caps retention and explains the baseline performance.
Machine-translated subtitles with errors and untranslated Chinese cards look cheap.
Huge mid-frame watermark and zoom-crop blur edges reduce quality.
Exposition dumps over a static split card (490-538) are the slowest stretch.
Uses a real trademarked AI brand name and logo as villain; avoid any real brand.

code_only_remake_needs.characters: Flat 2D cutout puppets in SVG: big oval head, swappable eye sets (normal dots, tiny-pupil white rings for fear, black-ringed blank eyes for hypnotised, angry brows), mouth flap with 3-4 visemes, 2-3 body poses (standing, holding phone to ear, running, lying in bed). 5-6 characters reuse one rig with hair/outfit swaps (hero yellow jacket, friend red hair, vendor chef hat, elder Tang jacket, doctor coat, suited leader).
code_only_remake_needs.backgrounds: Flat vector rooms with 2-3 tones each: bedroom with curtains, desk, repair shop with water dispenser, street stall brick wall, park fence street, alley with trash can, prison gate and cell bars, office with round table, hospital room, crowd silhouettes. Gaussian blur on the far layer for depth.
code_only_remake_needs.ui_inserts: Phone/caller-ID card (number + 'flagged as scam by N people' counter), app icon (eye with an animated swirl-vortex pupil: SVG radial gradient plus rotating spiral), laptop corner with Wi-Fi icon that vanishes, webcam window pop-up, CRT screen with typing dots, billboard text card. All of these are pure React/SVG components.
code_only_remake_needs.fx: Hypnotic spinning sigil (an original geometric knot, not a real logo) with glow; hyperspace streak tunnel (canvas radial lines) for memory floods; blue cyberspace grid plus light rays; energy-burst wipe; smoke puff; anger-mark and lightning sprites that pop with scale overshoot; red blinking dot; translucent sheet overlay; screen shake on scares; dutch tilt.
code_only_remake_needs.camera: Mostly static framing with digital punch-ins (scale 1.0 → 1.25) on reactions, about every 4 s; slow push-ins on reveals; hard cuts; background slide for running. A per-shot camera keyframe track in the storyboard is enough.
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Single fast first-person narrator via local TTS (Kokoro at about 1.25-1.35x to reach 280-300 wpm, alt voices for caller, friend and AI), continuous tense music bed, SFX for ringtone, jolt hits, whoosh on punch-ins, static for the recorder.
code_only_remake_needs.captions: Bottom band: bold white serif/sans on a 60% black strip, 1-2 lines, sentence chunks synced to TTS timestamps. Avoid the reference's tiny size: use larger word-chunk captions for retention.
code_only_remake_needs.structure_template: Rule-based tech-possession story: inciting 4 AM call with rule → 4-5 escalating rule-test set pieces (each about 20-40 s) → chase → public villain reveal → dead-mentor twist → backstory → sacrifice → 'was it a dream' → loop callback → test reveal → climax → sting with the villain inside the hero. Aim for ~6-10 min with twists every 60-90 s in the back half.
code_only_remake_needs.effort_estimate: Medium. One reusable puppet rig plus about 10 backgrounds and about 8 FX/UI components cover the whole video, because the reference's visual grammar is static shots with expression swaps and inserts.
